scoring_checks: The four one-point rows separately assess null-mass safety, supported-state balance under the actual uniform mixture, the passage to set fluxes, and the failure of the convergence implication. The authored proof earns all four points. The set-flux and counterexample rows already allow equivalent valid arguments.

Row 1 unnecessarily mandates using the supplied law at the supported atom to justify the reverse transition. The question does not require that route. For a concrete complete alternative, draw X from μ and fix a selected site i. Condition on R = X_{-i}; given any r with positive marginal probability, the original bit and the resampled bit are independent draws from the same conditional law. Thus the singleton pair flux at a common r is P(R=r) p_r(x_i) p_r(y_i), symmetric in x and y. Pairs with unequal retained tuples are impossible, marginal-null r contributes no flux, and a null atom on a positive fiber has zero conditional mass. Uniform averaging gives all singleton balances, which can then be used in the same set-sum argument and followed by the same valid counterexample. This proof does not justify the reverse transition by applying the supplied pointwise positive-start law, so the literal first row could withhold credit from a complete proof.

Natural-language L3 is supported by the zero-mass and compatible-fiber cases, conversion of singleton balances to set fluxes, and a counterexample using the actual kernel. The finite law is given and no L4 domain, integrability, or error adapter is required.

Lean L3 is supported independently by the null and positive cases, correspondence between off-site agreement and retained tuples, and finite-sum algebra.
